outline.description: Introduce the problem of controlling large text-to-image diffusion models and the need for principled finetuning methods that preserve pretrained generative abilities while enabling downstream control.
subtopics: Why text guidance alone is insufficient for fine-grained control
Two target tasks: subject-driven generation and controllable generation
Desiderata for finetuning: training efficiency and generalizability preservation
Limitations of small-step finetuning and additive adapters
The core idea of OFT: preserving hyperspherical structure via orthogonal transformations

outline.description: Provide a concise primer on diffusion-based text-to-image systems and how they integrate text guidance, with emphasis on Stable Diffusion and related architectures used in the paper.
subtopics: Score-based and denoising diffusion models
Latent vs pixel-space diffusion (e.g., Stable Diffusion, Imagen, DALL·E 2)
Role of text encoders and cross-attention
Inference and conditioning mechanisms
Where finetuning acts in diffusion pipelines

outline.chapter_title: Existing Finetuning Strategies and Their Limits
outline.description: Survey common finetuning approaches for large generative models and pinpoint gaps that motivate OFT.
subtopics: Full finetuning with small learning rates
Adapter-based methods (e.g., LoRA, Adapters)
Task-specific controllers (ControlNet, T2I-Adapter)
Assumption of Euclidean proximity to pretrained weights
Need for a structural preservation measure beyond Euclidean distance

outline.chapter_title: Geometry of Neural Representations: Hyperspheres and Energy
outline.description: Introduce the geometric viewpoint that neuron directions encode semantics, and define hyperspherical energy as a measure of pairwise neuron relationships.
subtopics: Neuron normalization and cosine similarity
Hyperspherical energy: definition and interpretation
Energy, uniformity, and semantic preservation
Empirical evidence: angular features capture semantics
Toy autoencoder study: angle vs magnitude for reconstruction
Fourier phase vs magnitude analogy for semantics

outline.description: Explain why orthogonal transformations naturally preserve hyperspherical structure and are well-suited for controlled finetuning.
subtopics: Angle preservation under orthogonal transforms
Layer-shared transforms to maintain pairwise neuron angles
Regularization effect of orthogonality vs unconstrained rotations
Connections to orthogonal over-parameterized training
Why preserving (not minimizing) hyperspherical energy matters for finetuning

outline.description: Detail the OFT method: how it modifies forward passes, preserves hyperspherical energy, and adapts pretrained models without destroying semantics.
subtopics: OFT objective: preserve pairwise angular relations (hyperspherical energy invariance)
Layer-shared orthogonal matrices applied to pretrained weights
Initialization at identity to start from pretrained model
Applicability to fully-connected, attention, and convolutional layers
No inference overhead: folding transforms into weights post-training

outline.description: Cover practical parameterizations and efficiency considerations that make OFT scalable to large models.
subtopics: Cayley transform for differentiable orthogonality
Special orthogonal group limitation (determinant = 1) and practical relevance
Block-diagonal orthogonal matrices for parameter efficiency
Block sharing across channels/layers
Parameter complexity analysis vs LoRA
Implementation notes and stability considerations

outline.chapter_title: Constrained and Rescaled Variants: COFT and Re-Scaled OFT
outline.description: Introduce COFT for added stability with a deviation constraint, and re-scaled OFT to modestly increase flexibility while preserving energy.
subtopics: COFT: orthogonality plus radius constraint around identity
Constraining via the Cayley parameter Q with projected updates
Controlling flexibility with epsilon and its effects on behavior
Rescaled OFT: per-neuron positive scaling that leaves energy unchanged
When and why to prefer OFT vs COFT vs Rescaled OFT

outline.description: Explain how OFT integrates into DreamBooth-style pipelines for identity preservation and controllability with few subject images.
subtopics: Problem setup and training data
Loss functions and prior preservation (DreamBooth framework)
Where OFT is inserted (attention layers for fair comparison)
Stability across iterations and insensitivity to training length
Metrics: DINO, CLIP-I for subject fidelity; CLIP-T for prompt fidelity; LPIPS diversity
Quantitative and qualitative findings vs DreamBooth and LoRA

outline.description: Show how OFT enables controllability from external signals (edges, segmentation, landmarks) and outperform controller networks with fewer parameters.
subtopics: Control signals: Canny edges, segmentation maps, facial landmarks
Datasets: COCO (C2I), ADE20K (S2I), CelebA-HQ (L2F)
Training setup vs ControlNet and T2I-Adapter
Faster, smoother convergence and data efficiency
Qualitative comparisons: structure adherence and realism
No added inference-time compute compared to controller networks

outline.description: Detail the evaluation methodology used in the paper, including a new control consistency metric that aligns with downstream goals.
subtopics: Subject-driven metrics: DINO, CLIP-I, CLIP-T, LPIPS
Control consistency metrics:
- For edges: IoU and F1 between predicted and input edges
- For segmentation: mean IoU, mean/overall accuracy
- For landmarks: mean L2 distance
Convergence speed and stability tracking
Human evaluation considerations

outline.description: Provide a practical walkthrough for implementing OFT/COFT in modern diffusion models, including hyperparameter choices and troubleshooting.
subtopics: Which layers to finetune (e.g., attention matrices) for fair comparisons
Choosing block count and block sharing
Learning rate, iterations, and epsilon selection
Initialization (identity, zero for Q) and optimization steps
Parameter and memory budgeting vs adapters and controllers
Troubleshooting: instability without orthogonality, failure cases

outline.description: Deepen understanding through comparisons to LoRA and related concepts, and summarize empirical ablations from the paper.
subtopics: OFT as multiplicative vs LoRA as additive low-rank update
When OFT induces effective low rank via (R−I)W0
Convergence on hypersphere manifolds and smooth optimization landscapes
Why not minimize hyperspherical energy in finetuning
Ablations: removing orthogonality, varying epsilon, block sizes
Channel-wise interpretations for convolution (depthwise-like behavior)

outline.description: Discuss the bounds of the current approach and highlight research directions opened by OFT.
subtopics: Computational cost of Cayley inverse and scaling to very large layers
Compositionality of orthogonal transforms across tasks
Beyond block-diagonal parameterization for parameter efficiency
Potential for multi-task and modular finetuning via orthogonal composition
Integration with other control modalities and multi-conditioning
Bridging theory and practice: formalizing semantic preservation guarantees
